text: Unreal: Check the host and project
Save in .vscode/settings.json. Type unreal. in a Python file to check suggestions.
import unrealunreal.log("Hello from Unreal")print(unreal.SystemLibrary.get_engine_version())print(unreal.Paths.project_dir())

import unrealeditor = unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.EditorActorSubsystem)actors = editor.get_selected_level_actors()print("Selected Actors:", len(actors))for actor in actors:    print(actor.get_actor_label(), actor.get_class().get_name())
get_selected_level_actors() returns Actor objects. len counts them; the loop reads each label and class.

import unrealassets = unreal.EditorUtilityLibrary.get_selected_assets()print("Selected assets:", len(assets))for asset in assets:    print(asset.get_name(), asset.get_class().get_name())    print(asset.get_path_name())
Read compression and sRGB. Non-texture selections are counted and skipped.

import unrealfrom pathlib import Pathdisk_folder = Path(unreal.Paths.project_dir()) / "Content"object_path = "/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube.Cube"mesh = unreal.load_asset(object_path)print("Disk folder:", disk_folder)print("Loaded object:", mesh.get_path_name() if mesh else None)print("Content directory exists:", disk_folder.is_dir())
bpy.context.selected_objects supplies Blender Objects. Unreal uses its own editor APIs.
